subject: Novus Health renewal — marketplace entitlement handoff & invoicing
messages:
From: Samantha Leung <samantha.leung@novushealth.org>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@novushealth.org>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal timing & marketplace option questions

Hi Jonas,

Our annual renewal is coming up for the enterprise plan (term ends 2027-07-31). Procurement asked whether Novus can move to marketplace billing for the renewal — they prefer Marketplace invoicing tied to our existing Azure marketplace contract.

A few quick questions:
- Does moving to the Azure Marketplace change list price or discount tiers for committed capacity?
- Will usage/overage still be reported in the same way so our finance team can reconcile?
- Any special entitlements or SKUs we need to accept in the marketplace?

I attached the latest SOW for reference. Could you outline the technical steps and any timeline constraints?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Leung
Senior Procurement Manager
Novus Health

Attachment: Novus_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Leung <samantha.leung@novushealth.org>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal timing & marketplace option questions

Hi Samantha — thanks for the note and the SOW. Short answers up front: moving to Azure Marketplace will not change the committed unit pricing in your current renewal if we mirror the existing contract terms in the marketplace listing; it does change the invoicing flow (Marketplace invoice from Microsoft) and requires entitlement mapping for the SKU.

Suggested kickoff steps (high level):
1) Confirm which Redwood SKU to map to your commitment — see attached entitlement map.
2) Finance/Procurement to confirm acceptance of Microsoft invoice flow and tax handling.
3) We prepare an amendment + marketplace listing change (DocuSign).
4) Cutover: provision marketplace entitlements and test one small renewal invoice in staging.

Timeline: we can get amendment + DocuSign ready in 3 business days once legal/finance sign off; marketplace propagation to Azure usually 5–7 business days.

I'll loop in Karthik (finance) and Laura (renewals lead) to scope the DocuSign and any billing credit required for the switch. Do you have a target cutover date?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Marketplace_Entitlement_Map.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal timing & marketplace option questions

Team — quick internal alignment:
- Karthik: can you confirm if Novus qualifies for the same committed discount tiers under the marketplace SKU? If not, what do we need to do to preserve pricing?
- Ben (legal/ops): please prepare a minimal amendment that authorizes Redwood to issue entitlements via Azure marketplace and routes invoicing to Microsoft, with language for tax/responsibility.

If we want a July 1 cutover (customer preference), we need DocuSign by 2027-06-18 to give Azure time to onboard. I'll draft the amendment skeleton and drop it in the drive.

Laura Bennett
Renewals Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal timing & marketplace option questions

Laura — confirmed: Novus is within our definitional tier for committed discount parity. We can preserve the effective per-unit price by applying an internal credit during the first marketplace invoice cycle if needed; finance will reconcile on our side. Two notes:
- We need Alex Cho (Novus finance) to sign off that Microsoft invoicing is acceptable for their internal PO workflows.
- Please include explicit language about who is responsible for overage billing timing (Microsoft vs Redwood) — avoids double-billing risk.

I'll prepare the accounting move and a short write-up for Procurement to include with DocuSign.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Leung <samantha.leung@novushealth.org>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Cho <alex.cho@novushealth.org>, procurement@novushealth.org
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal timing & marketplace option questions

Jonas — this looks good, thank you. A couple follow-ups from procurement/finance:
- Alex confirms marketplace invoicing is acceptable but wants a short note on how line items will appear on the Microsoft invoice (we need SKU + quantity + period).
- Can you confirm whether the marketplace entitlement requires us to accept terms in the Azure portal or if the DocuSign amendment is sufficient?
- We would like a one-time credit to account for a month overlap due to our internal PO cycle (June 30 invoice period). Is Redwood able to provide a pro-rata credit for June?

If you can send the DocuSign draft and a sample Microsoft invoice rendering, we can push this through procurement quickly.

Samantha
